lesson.title: Diminutive Gym
lesson.subtitle: broodje, kopje, huisje, appeltje, bloemetje, hondje

hook.title: Six Shapes of Small
hook.content: Broodje, kopje, huisje, appeltje, hondje, tafeltje: six nouns, six diminutive shapes, one article. The ending changes; het does not.

pattern.title: Choose the allomorph, keep het
pattern.content: Broodje and kopje take -je; huisje takes -je; appeltje takes -tje; hondje takes -je; tafeltje takes -tje. The final sound decides the shape.
pattern.trap_note: The diminutive is not only for small things. It can soften a request or make a word friendly: een kopje koffie is a normal cup, not a tiny one.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Diminutive Gym):
exercises.target_answer: het broodje, het kopje, het huisje, het appeltje, het hondje, het tafeltje
exercises.meaning: bread roll; sandwich, small cup, little house, little apple, little dog, little table
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Diminutive Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “The roll is fresh.”?
exercises.explanation: “Het broodje is vers.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Diminutive Gym”.

cues: The pattern: Choose the allomorph, keep het
It means: The cup is small.
exercises.explanation: “Het kopje is klein.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Choose the allomorph, keep het.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: The diminutive is not only for small things. It can soften a request or make a word friendly: een kopje koffie is a normal cup, not a tiny one.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
options: not The little house is old.
exercises.explanation: “Het huisje is oud.” is word-for-word “The little house is old.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Choose the allomorph, keep het.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: The little apple is red.
exercises.explanation: “Het appeltje is rood.” reuses only material taught in “Diminutive Gym” — Choose the allomorph, keep het.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Het appeltje is rood.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Choose the allomorph, keep het.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “The little table is big.”
twist.explanation: Tafel → tafeltje; the diminutive is het even when the object is big.

summary.outcome: Produce the common diminutive allomorphs and keep the article het.
summary.takeaway: The diminutive ending is predictable from the noun's final sound; the article is always het.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Capstone: De Brug Reading.

broodje.etymology_derivation: Diminutive of brood; every diminutive is het.

kopje.etymology_derivation: Diminutive of kop; the -je makes it het.

huisje.etymology_derivation: Diminutive of huis; the -je makes it het.

appeltje.etymology_derivation: Diminutive of appel; the -tje makes it het.

hondje.etymology_derivation: Diminutive of hond; the -je makes it het.

tafeltje.etymology_derivation: Diminutive of tafel; the -tje makes it het.
